    AI Overview
    As of late March 2026, 30-year FHA loan rates generally hover in the high-5% to mid-6% range, with many lenders offering rates around 5.8%–6.1% for qualified borrowers
    . FHA loans, ideal for low-to-moderate-income buyers, require a 3.5% down payment for credit scores of 580 or higher. 
    Current FHA Loan Rate Trends (March 2026) 
    • 30-Year Fixed FHA: Rates often sit between 5.84% and 6.47%, depending on lender and credit score, with APRs higher due to mortgage insurance premiums.
    • 15-Year Fixed FHA: Typically lower, ranging closer to 5.49%–5.99%.
    • Refinance Rates: 30-year FHA refinance rates are currently around 5.88%–5.99%. 
    Key Considerations for FHA Loans 
    • Minimum Credit Score: Generally 580 for a 3.5% down payment, though some lenders may allow lower scores with a 10% down payment.
    • Mortgage Insurance: FHA loans require an upfront mortgage insurance premium (1.75%) and an annual premium (0.55%) paid monthly.
    • Loan Limits: Rates are for loans within Federal Housing Administration limits, which vary by county.
    • Rate Factors: Factors affecting your specific rate include your credit score, down payment size, and the purchase price of the home. 
    Rates are subject to daily change, and borrowers should check with multiple lenders for the best available option.

    Is FHA 3.5% down?
    FHA loans have lower credit and down payment requirements for qualified homebuyers. For instance, the minimum required down payment for an FHA loan is only 3.5% of the purchase price. The FHA mortgage calculator includes additional costs in the estimated monthly payment.
